summary: About five hours after the Poblacion 7 fire on Friday, 24 January 2025, a separate fire razed three houses in the neighbouring Barangay Rosary Heights 10, Cotabato City. Philstar, citing the BFP and the city disaster office, reported the two fires gutted 103 houses in all; no casualties, cause or family count were given, and the city social welfare office distributed relief to victims at evacuation sites.

sources.title: 103 houses razed in Cotabato

note: Philstar says the second fire came five hours after the first, not about 10 hours as the record said.

summary: A US military-contracted Beechcraft King Air 300 (N349CA), flying from Cebu toward Cotabato City on an aerial survey, was seen flying low before it nose-dived into an open rice field in Barangay Malatimon, Ampatuan, Maguindanao del Sur at about 2 p.m. on Thursday, 6 February 2025. All 4 aboard, a US Marine and 3 defence contractors, were killed; Maguindanao del Sur police recovered the bodies from the wreckage and the CAAP opened an investigation.

sources.title: US military contracted aircraft crashes in Maguindanao del Sur, killing 4 passengers

barangay: 17 nautical miles southeast of the Turtle Islands
summary: The wooden-hulled M/L Bangsata left Turtle Islands at about 1:45 a.m. on Sunday, 16 March 2025 bound for South Ubian, Tawi-Tawi with 32 people aboard, met rough seas and sank at about 6 a.m. The Singaporean-flagged tanker Eonia spotted the survivors and alerted authorities; the Navy's BRP Jose Loor Sr. (PC-390) picked up 26 of them some 17 nautical miles southeast of the Turtle Islands at about 10:05 p.m. and a Malaysian vessel rescued the other 6. No one died or went missing, and the survivors were turned over to the MDRRMO at Taganak Pier.

summary: A motorboat skippered by Alsappa Gayong, carrying 5 people to Poblacion, Sapa-Sapa, Tawi-Tawi for an Islamic ceremony at the MSU covered court, was battered by huge waves from the southwest monsoon and capsized at about 11:11 a.m. on Friday, 22 August 2025 between the islands of Mantabuan and Latuan. All 5 were rescued by about noon, the Sapa-Sapa MDRRMO said; one of them, stung by a stingray, was given first aid and taken to Tuan Ligaddung Lipae Memorial Hospital.

summary: The motor launch M/L Nurdia, carrying 30 people (16 men, 9 women and 5 children, among them a pregnant woman and two senior citizens), was found drifting with a rudder damaged in rough seas about 46 nautical miles east of Taganak Island, Turtle Islands, Tawi-Tawi on the evening of Friday, 16 January 2026. A Western Mindanao Naval Command patrol craft on routine patrol spotted its flashing light, took everyone off unharmed and turned them over to the local government at Taganak on Saturday, 17 January, where they were given food, water and medical checks.

summary: The Aleson Shipping ro-pax ferry MV Trisha Kerstin 3, sailing from Zamboanga City to Jolo with more than 340 passengers and crew, took on water, listed and sank about 2.75 nautical miles northeast of Baluk-Baluk Island, Hadji Muhtamad, Basilan at about 1:50 a.m. on Monday, 26 January 2026. The Coast Guard recovered bodies for weeks: by 22 February the toll stood at 65 dead, 293 rescued and 14 missing, and the PCG completed a full underwater search of the wreck on 24 February. By 29 July 2026 the Inquirer put the dead at 66 and reported Aleson still suspended and fined P3 million.

summary: Two fisherfolk were rescued on Sunday, 15 February 2026 after their 8-metre fishing boat capsized in rough seas off Lantawan, Basilan. They drifted for about two hours until the passing M/L Sea Dayang spotted them at 11 a.m. and alerted the Coast Guard's BRP Melchora Aquino, whose rigid-hull inflatable boat picked them up; both were in stable condition after first aid and a check with the PDRRMO, and were taken to the PCG Sub-Station Lantawan.

note: Day and details from the Manila Bulletin search snippet (host refuses fetches). SunStar's '2 fishermen rescued off Basilan' (5 Feb 2026) is a different incident off Baluno, Isabela City on 4 February.

summary: A fire broke out at 10:09 p.m. on Tuesday, 3 February 2026 in the coastal village of Lamion, Bongao, Tawi-Tawi and burned for about four hours through around 1,000 stilt houses mostly of light materials, displacing some 5,000 people, before the Bongao Central Fire Station declared it out at about 2 a.m. The MDRRMO reported no deaths; the cause and damage estimate were under investigation. Bongao was placed under a state of calamity, and the Bangsamoro government later gave cash aid to over 900 fire-hit households.

summary: Five elementary pupils aged 7 to 11, three boys and two girls, drowned around noon on Thursday, 16 April 2026 while swimming in a pond-like water impounding area at Phase 2 of the permanent shelter in Barangay Panoroganan, Marawi City, far from any houses. Police said they had been floating on a discarded refrigerator that tipped over in the deep part; a playmate aged 8 was rescued and given first aid. All five were declared dead on arrival at a Marawi hospital. The Inquirer placed the site in Barangay Kilala and dated it 15 April.

summary: A fire broke out shortly before midnight on Wednesday, 19 August 2026 at the public market in Barangay Poblacion, Shariff Aguak, Maguindanao del Sur, and was put out at about 1:45 a.m. on 20 August. A married couple, believed to have been asleep in their stall, were found dead inside it; 8 to 10 stalls were affected, including some selling LPG, and several cylinders exploded. The BFP's initial assessment pointed to an electrical cause, with the investigation ongoing.
